reference.source: OMIM / GeneReviews / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A treatable riboflavin transporter defect: consider it in any child or young adult with progressive sensorineural deafness combined with a motor neuronopathy, because timely riboflavin supplementation can arrest and partly reverse the course
Caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the riboflavin transporter genes SLC52A2 (RFVT2) or SLC52A3 (RFVT3), inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern
The hallmark is a pontobulbar palsy: progressive bulbar weakness with dysphagia, dysarthria, facial and tongue wasting, plus sensorineural hearing loss
Additional features include limb weakness, optic atrophy, sensory ataxia, axial hypotonia and respiratory insufficiency, which can be life-limiting if untreated
Plasma flavin levels and an acylcarnitine profile resembling a multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenation defect may support the diagnosis, but a normal biochemical screen does not exclude it
High-dose oral riboflavin supplementation is the mainstay of treatment and should be started empirically on clinical suspicion rather than waiting for genetic confirmation
Fazio-Londe disease is regarded as the same disorder without prominent deafness, sitting on the same riboflavin-transporter spectrum
Response to riboflavin is often dramatic, so early recognition materially changes outcome
reference.pathophysiology: The syndrome arises from defective cellular uptake of riboflavin (vitamin B2) due to loss-of-function variants in the riboflavin transporter genes SLC52A2 and SLC52A3. Impaired riboflavin transport lowers tissue levels of the flavin cofactors FMN and FAD, which are essential for numerous flavoenzymes, particularly those of mitochondrial fatty-acid beta-oxidation and the respiratory chain. The resulting energy failure and oxidative stress preferentially injure cranial nerve motor nuclei, anterior horn cells and the auditory pathway, producing the characteristic progressive pontobulbar palsy with deafness. Because the defect is one of cofactor delivery rather than an irreparable structural lesion, supplying supraphysiological riboflavin can restore flavoenzyme activity and halt neurodegeneration.
additionalDifferentials: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and other motor neurone disease
Spinal muscular atrophy and Fazio-Londe disease
Multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (glutaric aciduria type II)
additionalInvestigations: Molecular genetic testing of SLC52A2 and SLC52A3
Plasma and, where available, tissue flavin (riboflavin/FAD) concentrations
Plasma acylcarnitine profile and urine organic acids looking for a MADD-like pattern
Audiometry and brainstem auditory evoked responses
Nerve conduction studies and electromyography to characterise the neuronopathy
redFlags: Progressive respiratory insufficiency or stridor from bulbar and diaphragmatic weakness
Rapidly advancing dysphagia with aspiration risk
Acute deterioration during intercurrent catabolic illness
Progressive visual loss from optic atrophy
reference.prognosis: Untreated disease is progressive and can be fatal from respiratory or bulbar failure, but early high-dose riboflavin supplementation frequently stabilises and partially reverses neurological deficits, so prognosis depends heavily on prompt recognition and treatment.
pitfalls: Mislabelling the presentation as motor neurone disease or a non-treatable neurodegeneration and missing a treatable cause
Delaying empirical riboflavin while awaiting genetic results
Assuming a normal plasma flavin or acylcarnitine profile excludes the diagnosis
Overlooking deafness as an early and pivotal diagnostic clue
references: OMIM entries for SLC52A2 and SLC52A3
management: Start high-dose oral riboflavin supplementation empirically on clinical suspicion to replenish FMN and FAD cofactors and restore flavoenzyme activity, without waiting for genetic confirmation
Provide swallowing assessment and nutritional support, with gastrostomy feeding where progressive bulbar weakness causes unsafe dysphagia
Monitor respiratory function and institute non-invasive ventilation and airway clearance as respiratory insufficiency develops
Offer auditory rehabilitation with hearing aids or cochlear implantation for the sensorineural hearing loss
Engage physiotherapy, occupational therapy and speech and language therapy for limb and bulbar weakness and communication needs
Monitor treatment response with serial neurological, audiometric and respiratory assessment alongside plasma flavin and acylcarnitine profiles
Coordinate care through a multidisciplinary neurology and metabolic medicine team
Provide genetic counselling and test siblings for biallelic SLC52A2 or SLC52A3 variants so affected relatives can begin riboflavin early
